Strictly confidential. All contents in this document are property of Kineton s.r.l. 2018 Introduction CAPL o The CAN Acc
slides.body:
o The CAN Access Programming Language (CAPL) is a C-Like programming
language, which allows you to quickly develop codes that make CANalyzer or
CANoe simulations more powerful.
o It is a procedural language whereby the execution of program blocks (Event
Procedures) is controlled on events.
o The code defined in the event procedures is executed when an event occurs,
i.e. you can send a message on the bus in response to a “key press” (on key),
track the occurrence of messages on the bus (on message), or execute certain
actions cyclically (on Timer).

slides.body:
Data Types available in CAPL are:
o Integers variables: int, int64, dword, word, char, byte
o Floating point numbers: float and double
o CAN messages and Timers
All variables can be initialized in their declarations, except for the timer. If a variable is not initialized,
the compiler will initialize the variable with default values (unless otherwise defined : 0 ).
o CAPL permits the declaration of arrays, analogous to their declaration in the C programming
language.

slides.body:
Once you have created a timer and it is expired, the function developed in the event on Timer is
executed.
o You can use this functionality to develop cyclic actions, or to respond to an event after a delay.
o The function setTimer() needs 2 parameters, the name of the timer and the length. The maximum
length varies according to the specified unit.
o The function setTimerCyclic() allows to execute cyclic actions without resetting the timer.
o Defining the timer as timer, it will be calculated each second, so the maximum value that can be
reached is 1799 seconds.
o Otherwise, using msTimer to define the timer, it will be calculated each millisecond, so the maximum
value available is 65535 milliseconds.
React to Time eventsCAPL

slides.body:
These events are used to perform actions before, at the start of, and after CANalyzer or CANoe
measurements.
o They can be called just once in the code
o The event on preStart is associated with the press of the “GO” button in CANalyzer or CANoe. It is
possible to initialize variables, read data from files or write something on the “write” window. Here, it
is impossible to send CAN messages onto the bus or set timers.
o After the preStart, all the actions in the on start can be performed. Here you can set Timers or send
messages onto the bus, and initialize environmental variables. The measurement is also started at
this time.
o When you press the “STOP” button, the on stopMeasurements event is executed. This way, you can
print statistics in the write window or output messages onto the bus or write a log file. After this event
is finished the measurement will be stopped.
React to System Events (preStart, Start, stopMeasurements)CAPL

Strictly confidential. All contents in this document are property of Kineton s.r.l. 2018 Goal INTRODUCTION 31 During V&V
slides.body:
GoalINTRODUCTION
During V&V activities on both vehicle and HIL, sometimes it is necessary to change signals
that ECUs send or receive on CAN bus.In some cases, the maneuvers to vary these signals
aren’t suitable to be replicated physically due to:
- Dangerous conditions for the driver
- Damages to vehicle components (sensors, actuators, wirings, ECUs)
- Difficult vehicular conditions
- Long-time or particular testing conditions
Others application cases could be:
- Loss of Communication (LoC) between real ECUs
- MC (Message Counter) and CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) errors (Implausibility Faults)
IG BLOCK and CAPL can be used for all those purposes

slides.body:
GoalCOMMON USES OF CAPL
⮚ To change the signal’s value of a specific cyclic and cyclic on event message
⮚ To set a Lost of Communication (LoC) between different ECUs
⮚ To set implausible data transmission/reception (MC, CRC, SNA or validity bit)
⮚ To change more signals of the same CAN bus at the same instant
⮚ To change signals belonging to different CAN buses (e.g. C1, ePT) → Double Gateway
